notes.roe: Reported ROE 8.3%; adjusted ROE was 10.6% for the quarter.
notes.efficiencyRatio: Reported (unadjusted) productivity ratio 62.1%; adjusted productivity ratio was 56.1%.
notes.netIncomeMillions: Net income attributable to common shareholders, reported basis; adjusted net income was $2,119 million.
notes.loansToAssetsPct: Computed from total loans ($760,829M) divided by total assets ($1,412,027M), both from the same press release.
notes.loanToDepositRatio: Gross loans $767,365mm (Note 14, before $6,536mm allowance) ÷ total deposits $943,849mm (Note 21), as at Oct 31, 2024. 2024 Annual Report, audited Consolidated Statement of Financial Position.
notes.wholesaleFundingPct: Computed: Table T58 'Total wholesale funding sources' $269,507mm (bank deposits, bearer deposit notes/CP/CDs, ABCP, senior notes, bail-inable notes, ABS, covered bonds, mortgage securitization, subordinated debentures — excludes repo per T58 footnote 1) plus 'Obligations related to securities sold under repurchase agreements and securities lent' $190,449mm (balance sheet) = $459,956mm, divided by total assets $1,412,027mm = 32.57%. Excluding repo (Scotiabank's own T58 scope only) the figure is 19.09%.
notes.wholesaleDepositsPct: Business & government ($600,114mm) + Financial institutions ($44,914mm) ÷ total deposits $943,849mm.
notes.stableDepositsPct: LCR Table T56, 'Retail deposits and deposits from small business customers — Stable deposits' unweighted value $100,986mm ÷ total balance-sheet deposits $943,849mm = 10.70%. Caution: T56 unweighted values represent only balances maturing or callable within the next 30 days — i.e. this excludes term/GIC deposits with longer residual maturity, so it understates the true share of total deposits that would ultimately be classified stable if a full LCR-style categorization covered 100% of the deposit book. Sum of the four LCR categories here ($527,773mm) is only ~56% of total deposits; the remainder (mostly longer-dated term deposits and secured wholesale funding) is not captured by this table.
notes.lessStableDepositsPct: T56 'Less stable deposits' unweighted value $142,492mm ÷ total deposits $943,849mm. Same 30-day-window caveat as stableDepositsPct applies.
notes.operationalDepositsPct: T56 'Operational deposits (all counterparties) and deposits in networks of cooperative banks' unweighted value $114,881mm ÷ total deposits $943,849mm. Same caveat applies.
notes.nonOperationalDepositsPct: T56 'Non-operational deposits (all counterparties)' unweighted value $169,414mm ÷ total deposits $943,849mm. Same caveat applies.
notes.irrbbEveSensitivityPct: Scotiabank discloses only two shock scenarios (not the full Basel six): an immediate/sustained parallel +100bp and -100bp shock across major currencies (Table T50). FY2024 pre-tax EVE impact: +100bp = -$1,338mm (most adverse); -100bp = +$780mm. Most adverse (-$1,338mm) ÷ Tier 1 capital $69,499mm (Q4 2024 Supplementary Regulatory Capital Disclosure) = -1.93%. This %-of-Tier-1 computation is ours; Scotiabank itself only discloses the raw dollar figures and states results are 'within Board-approved limits' without disclosing the limit or a capital-ratio framing.
notes.irrbbNiiSensitivityPct: Same +100bp parallel shock (Table T50): pre-tax 12-month NII impact = -$21mm (FY2024). Expressed as % of FY2024 reported net interest income ($19,252mm) = -0.11%. As % of Tier 1 capital instead: -0.03%. The -100bp scenario showed -$31mm (-0.16% of NII). [Re-based to % of Tier 1 capital = -0.03% (previously -0.11% of NII) for cross-bank consistency.]
notes.newMetricsSource: 2024 Scotiabank Annual Report (Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 21 Deposits; Table T50 Structural Interest Sensitivity; Table T56 Bank's average LCR; Table T58 Wholesale Funding); Q4 2024 Supplementary Regulatory Capital Disclosure (Tier 1 capital) — https://www.scotiabank.com/content/dam/scotiabank/corporate/BNS_Annual_Report_2024_EN.pdf

notes.irrbbNiiSensitivityPct: Same Table T23, +100bp parallel shock: 12-month NII impact = +$197mm ÷ Net Tier 1 capital $72,961mm = 0.27%. Re-based to % of Tier 1 capital for consistency with the other banks (Scotiabank itself frames this as a dollar amount).
notes.wholesaleFundingPct: Computed: Table T58 "Total wholesale funding sources" $298,214M (excludes repo per T58 footnote) + period-end "Obligations related to securities sold under repurchase agreements and securities lent" $238,663M (Consolidated Statement of Financial Position) = $536,877M ÷ total assets $1,521,500M = 35.29%. Both components disclosed quarterly in the Scotiabank Q2 2026 Report to Shareholders; matches Scotiabank's existing Q4 method. Excluding repo (T58's own scope): 19.6%.

irrbbDisclosureNote: Scotiabank discloses IRRBB every quarter in its Report to Shareholders MD&A (Table T23 'Structural interest sensitivity'), and again at fiscal year-end (Oct 31) in the Annual Report (Table T50) and the audited financial-statement notes. It shows only two prescribed shocks — an immediate, sustained +100bp and -100bp parallel rate shock across major currencies — not the full Basel/OSFI six-scenario set (no steepener, flattener, or short-rate shocks are separately disclosed publicly). Both ΔEVE (present value of net assets) and ΔNII (next-12-month net interest income) are shown, pre-tax, on a constant balance-sheet basis with no management-action mitigation assumed, broken out by Canadian dollar vs. other currencies. Scotiabank states results are within 'Board-approved limits' but does not disclose those limits or express the sensitivities as a percentage of any capital measure — the %-of-Tier-1-capital figures in this dataset are computed by us, not sourced directly.
irrbbDisclosureSourceName: Scotiabank Q3 2025 Report to Shareholders, MD&A, Table T23 'Structural interest sensitivity' (also Annual Report Table T50 at year-end)
